result.title: Lesion-Aware Attention for Mammography Segmentation with Heterogeneous Supervision
result.summary: Accurate lesion segmentation in mammography is important for computer-aided breast cancer diagnosis, but dense pixel-level annotations remain costly and limited. Existing public segmentation datasets usually cover only a small set of lesion types with manually delineated masks, whereas larger mammography datasets often provide only image-level diagnostic labels. This annotation mismatch makes it difficult to train segmentation models that can generalize to rare or weakly annotated lesion categories. To address this problem, we study open-vocabulary mammographic lesion segmentation under a mixed-supervision setting, where pixel-level masks are available for base lesion categories and image-level labels are available for a broader set of categories. We propose a two-branch framework that jointly learns from segmentation data and classification data. The segmentation branch learns lesion boundaries from annotated masks, while the classification branch introduces additional image-level semantic supervision. To better transfer image-level supervision to lesion-relevant regions, we further introduce a Lesion-wise Attentive Classifier that maintains category-specific feature prototypes and generates lesion-aware attention maps for foreground feature pooling. This design reduces the influence of background tissue and encourages more compact lesion representations. Experiments on multiple mammography datasets show that the proposed method consistently improves open-vocabulary segmentation baselines on both base and novel lesion categories, while reducing the gap to fully supervised models that require dense target-domain masks. Qualitative results further indicate that our method produces more complete lesion localization for small, low-contrast, and visually subtle mammographic findings.

AI.brief_summary: 提出双分支框架（分割分支＋分类分支）与 Lesion-wise Attentive Classifier，利用类别原型生成病灶感知注意力图进行前景池化，在混合监督下做开放词汇乳腺 X 线病灶分割。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于医学影像分割的领域应用，目标是缓解掩码标注稀缺，未涉及内部推理状态生成、视觉证据筛选或停止决策等 LVR 问题，注意力池化也仅服务于分割监督迁移，缺少可核查的机制借鉴线索。
